Ignore the parallel-QA experiment docs. Be as autonomous as possible. End goal: a ready product after the first full end-to-end QA.
approved_decisions: Scope = M1-M4 (foundation+visibility, signals, owned sessions, orchestrator). M4.5/M5/M6 out of scope.
Cross-platform behind the D2 seam; Linux is the live, QA'd path. macOS drivers written but unverified. .pkg deferred.
Jira/Notion credentials deferred by the user; moot for M1-M4.
Parallel-QA experiment (docs/methodology/*) is OFF. QA runs once, after build and review.
LLM verdict lane stays deferred per spec D34.
Per spec section 0, each milestone gets its own plan -> implementation cycle. This PLAN is scoped to M1 only.

intent.goal: Ship M1 of Shepherd: foundation + visibility. Both daemons (controld, sessiond), the hookd dispatcher, hook ingest folding into session columns (D24), four tables (workspace, repo, session, app_state) with forward-only migrations, workspace/repo discovery and cwd->repo longest-prefix binding (D22), the workspace->session->subagent tree, the fleet page, and SSE. Read-only, attached sessions only.
non_goals: Owned sessions, tmux runner, spawn, terminal I/O, mailbox, ask() (M3).
The 7-bucket outcome palette, stop-reason classification, next_actions[], replay (M2).
Tool registry, MasterRuntime, authorize(), approvals, audit, chat page (M4).
work_item and queue tables, providers, reconcile, workers, matrix view (M5).
constraints: Python 3.12, mypy --strict, no Any (principle 6). Files past ~600 lines signal over-scope.
Principle 4: hooks time out, swallow all exceptions, always exit 0. Never harm Claude Code.
Principle 1: one direction, one store. No consumer gets a private read path into engine state.
D24: no event store. Fold hook events into session columns on arrival, then discard.
D25: evidence/audit/replay go to rotating JSONL logs, never the database. Readers skip malformed trailing lines.
D26/D33: all SQL lives in store/. store/ exposes domain verbs returning dataclasses; no caller passes SQL, receives a driver row, or opens a transaction.
Two processes: controld (restartable) and sessiond (long-lived). sessiond never migrates; it waits for controld to report the schema version over the UDS.
Section 13: loopback only, Origin-checked mutations, UDS at mode 0600 plus a per-boot token, no shell=True, never return a raw DB row, escape every innerHTML interpolation.
Host is Linux and there is no node/npm/tsc. The frontend must be plain ES modules served as-is.
Platform-dependent paths (state dir, credential store, service supervision) go behind a seam with a Linux driver as the live path.
Principle 5: unknown is first-class, counted and displayed.
acceptance_criteria: controld and sessiond both start on Linux, controld applies migrations in one transaction, and sessiond refuses to migrate.
A migration checksum mismatch refuses to start; a DB version newer than the binary refuses to start.
hookd.py writes a hook payload to sessiond's UDS with a 250ms timeout and exits 0 even when the socket is absent, the payload is malformed, or the write blocks.
A real hand-launched claude session registers itself as an attached session on SessionStart, binding cwd to the innermost registered repo by longest-prefix match.
Arriving hook events fold into session columns: last_event_at, state, needs_you_reason, tasks_done/tasks_total, active_subagents. No event row is stored.
Absent hook fields degrade their column to null rather than raising; the UI hides the corresponding chip.
The fleet page renders workspace -> session -> subagent, ordered needs_you -> running -> stopped -> idle, with no polling.
GET /api/events streams SSE with a monotonic seq; a client reconnecting with Last-Event-ID gets the gap replayed.
Hook write volume under concurrent sessions is measured and recorded (section 18 probe).
mypy --strict passes on the whole package and the test suite is green.

patterns: Pure core + IO shell enforced by AST repo-rules tests
